doc.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Music publishers like Max Dreyfus versus today's business
summary: Ingham compares old publishing houses with schooled editors, such as Max Dreyfus, to today's industry.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: schooled musicians, who would sort of look at a song and say well is this worthy of our house publishing it?

Like a book, exactly. I mean the famous one, I think it was — who was the publishers of the Cole Porter things? Anyway, famous, one of those companies. And they had a guy called Max Dreyfus who was famous — I mean he was an accomplished pianist, brilliant musician. I mean he could spot a well constructed song. He was Jerome Kern’s amanuensis. I mean he was responsible. He brought Gershwin in there, I mean all these people, they really knew quality. But like you say, like book publishing, you had an editor who could actually read you know, somebody who was literate. That’s very true. That’s a very good analogy. And that’s all gone now. What makes a hit now, I don’t know. I mean it’s just music.
